Memory.value: When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once
The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to

Negative Appraisals.value: My body keeps reacting as if I am still in danger even when I am safe
The world is a dangerous place
I was betrayed by someone I trusted

issues.item: Contamination: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened
issues.explanation: The contamination appraisal is hard to reconcile with the trauma type of police violence in this profile. It is much more characteristic of sexual trauma or interpersonal violation with a strong disgust/shame component, and here there are no supporting memory, trigger, threat, or strategy items that would make this appraisal clinically coherent. The remaining items describe intrusive, alien, uncontrolled traumatic memory and general danger/body-reactivity beliefs, which fit severe PTSD, but the contamination item stands out as a trauma-incongruent appraisal.

vignette: Sara is a 28-year-old police officer who recently experienced an incident during her shift that has left her struggling with intrusive memories and negative appraisals. Sara had been on duty when she witnessed another officer using excessive force against an unarmed individual. The event was traumatic, as she felt helpless to intervene effectively and saw the full impact of violence unfold in front of her eyes. Since then, the memory has become a potent trigger for her distress. The memories are particularly vivid and overwhelming; whenever they surface, Sara feels like she is reliving every sensory detail—the sights, sounds, smells, and even the physical sensations of fear and shock. These memories intrude at unexpected moments, often when she least expects it, such as during routine patrol or while on a date with her partner. The memory's intrusion can be so intense that Sara feels like it belongs to someone else rather than herself, leaving her questioning whether this is really what happened. Sara’s perception of the world has been deeply affected by these memories. She now views her body as an enemy, reacting in ways she cannot control—her heart races and she sweats profusely even when there is no immediate threat. This heightened state of arousal makes her feel perpetually unsafe, reinforcing her belief that the world is indeed a dangerous place. Her trust has been shattered; she feels betrayed by someone she once trusted, adding another layer of emotional pain to her experiences. The memories and negative appraisals are intertwined in Sara’s experience. When she remembers the incident, the vividness and intensity of the memory exacerbate her negative beliefs about herself and the world. The more these intrusive thoughts emerge, the stronger her feelings of betrayal and danger become. Conversely, when Sara feels the world is dangerous, it triggers her memories to resurface, making them feel even more alienating and overwhelming. This cycle has taken a toll on both Sara’s professional life and personal relationships. At work, she finds herself distracted and less confident in her abilities, sometimes avoiding certain patrol areas where she fears another incident might occur. This avoidance behavior has led to tensions with her colleagues who depend on her presence during critical situations. In her relationship, Sara struggles to open up about what she is going through; the fear of burdening her partner or being misunderstood keeps her from sharing her true feelings. What finally brought Sara to seek help was a series of minor incidents at work where her focus had waned due to intrusive memories. She realized that she could no longer maintain her usual performance level and feared making a critical mistake under pressure. Despite the weight of these experiences, Sara is hopeful for support and guidance in navigating through them. Sara’s most pressing fear now is losing control over her life—both professionally and personally—and being unable to trust others again. She hopes to find ways to regain a sense of safety and normalcy, believing that with help, she can break the cycle of intrusive memories and negative appraisals that have been dominating her life since the traumatic event.
